summary: Iter15 — Dual-auth (httpOnly cookie + Bearer header) + CSRF (double-submit cookie) migration verified end-to-end. Backend: 112 passed + 1 skipped — full regression iter11→iter18 (87) + iter14_refactors (4) + iter15_csrf_cookies (7) + iter15_csrf_extra (5 NEW probes I added on /api/employees, /api/admin/companies/*/switch, login exempt). Frontend smoke (Gov admin): login lands at /dashboard; both cookies set with EXACTLY the required attributes (access_token httpOnly=true secure=true sameSite=None; salonehcm_csrf httpOnly=false secure=true sameSite=None); CSRF probe via raw fetch confirms 403 without header + non-403 with header; axios interceptor attaches X-CSRF-Token on every state-changing /api/* call from the UI (0 UI POST/PUT/DELETE observed missing both csrf+auth); logout clears BOTH cookies in the browser context; redirect to /login. Superadmin 2FA path: TOTP login succeeds with cookies set correctly; /api/admin/companies/{cid}/switch returns 200, returns csrf_token in body, and refreshes BOTH cookies (verified via pytest with requests.Session — subsequent /api/auth/me with the new cookie returns the new company_id). The 2 console errors observed during testing are from MY OWN deliberate probe fetches (a 403 sans-CSRF + a 422 minimal-body create) — NOT real app errors.
critical_code_review_comments: core.py:100-120 csrf_protect is correct double-submit. Skips on safe methods, Bearer header, no-cookie, and login/accept-invite suffix. Uses secrets.compare_digest — constant-time, good. _CSRF_EXEMPT_SUFFIXES is endpoint-suffix matching (endswith) — works because the only ambiguity would be a router named '/auth/login' which doesn't exist elsewhere.

core.py:61-80 get_current_user reads cookie first then Bearer. Strips _id + password_hash via projection. company_id assertion is good — prevents orphaned/superadmin-without-tenant tokens from reaching tenant queries.

routers/auth.py:18-32 _set_auth_cookies — both cookies use max_age=43200 (12h) matching the JWT exp; samesite=None+secure=True is the correct browser policy for cross-site preview hosts. Logout uses delete_cookie path='/' which emits Max-Age=0 properly (verified live + via test_logout_clears_both_cookies).

routers/admin.py switch_company (per request) refreshes both cookies AND returns csrf_token in JSON — verified end-to-end via test_admin_switch_company_refreshes_cookies: new access_token cookie value differs, new csrf cookie value differs, and /api/auth/me with the new cookie returns the new company_id.

Bearer-auth bypass is necessary for backwards-compat with the 105 pre-existing test suite that uses Authorization: Bearer + sessionStorage. The risk surface is acceptable because (a) Bearer tokens still require valid JWT signature, (b) the cookie path is strictly opt-in for browsers via withCredentials, and (c) when both cookie + Bearer are present the Bearer wins (test_mixed_auth_prefers_authorization_header), which is the right default for SDK/CLI clients.

CORS allow_origin_regex on server.py:76-92 (*.preview.emergentagent.com with allow_credentials=True) is permissive but ACCEPTABLE for the preview environment. In production this regex must be tightened to a closed list of allowed origins, otherwise any subdomain that runs malicious JS could initiate authenticated cross-site requests. Flag for prod hardening — NOT a blocker for this iteration.

frontend/src/lib/api.js — request interceptor MUST be applied globally on the axios instance (verified: 0 UI state-changes observed missing CSRF in network capture). Watch for direct fetch() calls or window.location-based blob downloads that bypass axios; per the user request note these are gotchas but I did not observe any during smoke. Recommend a targeted lint rule banning raw fetch() outside the api.js wrapper.

Pre-existing carry-overs from previous iterations remain: test_iter6_batchB.py, test_salonehcm.py, parts of test_iter8_phase_abc.py + test_iter9_features.py have stale fixtures (admin role 'admin' vs current 'superadmin'; twilio_configured False vs True). NOT regressions from iter15.

The pre-existing 17 stale-fixture test failures (iter6_batchB, salonehcm, parts of iter8/iter9 expecting admin@salonehcm.sl role='admin' or twilio_configured=False) are NOT in scope for iter15 and carry over from prior iterations. rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in iter15 scope. One non-blocking browser-side observation during testing: an evaluate() chain that did POST /switch then immediately fetch /auth/me sometimes returned the old company_id in the same JS context. This is a browser fetch/cookie-jar propagation quirk in raw fetch chains, NOT a backend bug — the pytest equivalent using requests.Session demonstrates conclusively that after /switch the new access_token cookie carries the new company_id, and the real SPA does a page reload after switching tenants which avoids this quirk entirely.
